place_fields.summary: Pandavara Betta near Tumakuru is a relatively unexplored hill with unmarked trails, steep sections, slippery rocks and large boulders; recent trek reports describe it as challenging and recommend avoiding solo attempts because of navigation and wildlife risks.

planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The mapped attraction is at 9565+255, on an unnamed road in Mutsandra, Karnataka 572104.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The trail is unmarked and can involve steep ascents, slippery rocks, large boulders and wildlife; recent local trek reports advise against going alone.

place_fields.micro_region: Sri Siddaganga Kshetra, Aralihalli, Tumakuru district, Karnataka
place_fields.summary: RD Hills View Point is a viewpoint on the Ramadevara Betta climb, with panoramic views around the hill area. Ramadevara Betta is reached by a substantial stair climb followed by a shorter rocky approach to higher viewpoints.

planning_attributes.description: Viewpoint associated with the Ramadevara Betta hill climb.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The listing is at 85F6+HG8, Climbing Ramadevara Betta, Sri Siddaganga Kshetra, Aralihalli, Karnataka 572104.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Ramadevara Betta access has historically been controlled through the sanctuary; published visitor information lists daytime access around 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The climb involves hundreds of steps and the higher viewpoint uses a rocky section; take care on steep or exposed surfaces.

place_fields.vibe: forested hill, temple and sunrise viewpoint
place_fields.summary: DD Hills, or Devarayanadurga, is a forested granite hill area with viewpoints, fort remains and Narasimha temples. The summit is reached by road followed by a stair climb, and the area is known for panoramic views and sunrise visits.

planning_attributes.description: Devarayanadurga, commonly called DD Hills, is a hill destination near Tumakuru with the Yoga Narasimha temple at the summit and Bhoga Narasimha temple at the base.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The name Devarayanadurga means Devaraya's fort; the hill was renamed after Mysore ruler Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar and has fort and temple remains.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The hill is about 17 km from Tumakuru city by road; visitors can drive most of the way toward the summit and then climb stairs to the top.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Published visitor guidance says the hill itself has no general entry fee, while temple opening hours can differ from access to the hill and may change.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The trail and summit can be rocky and monkeys are commonly reported; use care on exposed viewpoints and carry water.
